issue: Capability failure leaves `batch.status` as running, and a later successful retry does not clear its stale `control.attention`, violating the lifecycle contract and leaving completed state with failure attention
reason: Verified in current source and within PRD 00007; bounded regression task carries this finding verbatim.

issue: `ovcaq run --no-tui` and `ovcaq capability retry agoge` always select an unavailable capability runner, so required capabilities can never succeed through the installed public commands
reason: Confirmed limitation, owned by PRD 00010. PRD 00007 P05-T06 explicitly requires the lifecycle against a fake; the coverage manifest assigns required real agoge execution and independent retry to 00010, whose provisioned execution proof integrates the real launcher runner. Keep the failure visible; do not introduce launcher-specific execution before that phase.

issue: Extract timeout-observation construction from `_collect`; the new function is 54 lines and exceeds the 50-line limit
reason: Verified in current source and within PRD 00007; bounded regression task carries this finding verbatim.

issue: Retry budgets can be dodged forever. `Supervisor._decide` resets `RetryState` whenever the failure class changes, and failure-path RETRY/WAIT decisions never advance `phase_repeats`. Alternating failures (agent death, then connectivity, then agent death...) therefore relaunch sessions without limit. This breaks the PRD's "Retry storms: Bound every wait/retry" mitigation. Confirmed by tracing `decide` and `_decide`
reason: Verified in current source and within PRD 00007; bounded regression task carries this finding verbatim.

issue: No production code ever starts a batch. Nothing in `src/` writes `batch.id` or `batch.status="running"`, and `new_state` leaves `batch.id=""`. So `ovcaq init` followed by `ovcaq run --no-tui` raises at `_open_session` → `publish_session_metric` → `_validate_identifier("")`, and `archive_final_state` also requires the id. The installed drain acceptance test passes only because its SEED script writes the batch fields straight through StateStore
reason: Verified in current source and within PRD 00007; bounded regression task carries this finding verbatim.

issue: A bootstrap repeat-stall (no PRD) returns PAUSE with exit 0 and writes no pause intent; the plan (§12.3 step 11) says halt. CI reads it as success, and every rerun burns another session before pausing again (test asserts `(0, PAUSE, 3)`)
reason: Requirements conflict: accepted design and task 1 explicitly specify bootstrap repeat PAUSE, while plan section 12.3 says bootstrap halt. The implementation matches the reviewed design. Preserve the existing behavior until the plan/design policy is reconciled; record the zero exit and missing durable intent limitation.

issue: `StateService.resume` always clears `pause_reason` but leaves `work.phase/next_phase == "paused"`. After a systemic park (records.py:445) or a `review_cap` pause, it erases the reason and the review_cap routing key that `workflow/resume.py:17` reads. Meanwhile `_boundary` still returns PAUSE, so `ovcaq run` exits 0 with 0 sessions and no explanation
reason: Verified in current source and within PRD 00007; bounded regression task carries this finding verbatim.

issue: The batch status lifecycle is incomplete. `apply(COMPLETE)` only archives, so a drain with no *required* capability (non-empty drain, or empty drain with only optional pending capabilities) archives `batch.status` still `running`. A failed capability never sets `batch.status="attention"`, which plan §8.6 step 5 requires
reason: Verified in current source and within PRD 00007; bounded regression task carries this finding verbatim.

issue: Capability timeout comes from the workflow phase route (`resolve_phase_route(work.phase or next_phase)`), not from capability config (plan §7 `[capabilities.agoge] timeout_seconds`). Startup `_reconcile_capabilities` resolves a full agent route (it needs agent config and a valid tier, and raises on phase `paused`) only to throw the timeout away
reason: Verified in current source and within PRD 00007; bounded regression task carries this finding verbatim.

issue: Reports count capability metric rows as workflow sessions. Canonical rows always carry `phase_launched` (None for capabilities) and `_metric_partitions` selects sessions by key presence. One capability attempt therefore inflates the session count and turns batch cost/token totals to unknown. No test covers it (test_canonical_metrics only has phase rows)
reason: Verified in current source and within PRD 00007; bounded regression task carries this finding verbatim.

issue: `_metric_partitions` silently drops any row whose `usage` is not a Mapping, using a `for usage in [...] if isinstance(...)` comprehension trick. That swallows an error and is hard to read
reason: Verified in current source and within PRD 00007; bounded regression task carries this finding verbatim.

issue: Extra `reconcile_metrics` calls. `CapabilityService._begin` rebuilds the aggregate right after publishing the pending row, so the aggregate shows the live capability attempt as `interrupted` for its whole run. `Supervisor._run_capability` calls it again after `finish`→`_finalize` already did
reason: Verified in current source and within PRD 00007; bounded regression task carries this finding verbatim.

issue: `Supervisor._run_capability` duplicates CapabilityService. It hand-builds `SessionPaths` that `_begin` already returned and `start` threw away, and re-implements `retry`'s run/finish-on-exception flow with a different failure detail (bare `str(error)` vs "runner raised …; retry X explicitly")
reason: Verified in current source and within PRD 00007; bounded regression task carries this finding verbatim.

issue: `_ResolvedModelClaudeDriver` inverts the tier map to turn the supervisor's resolved model back into a tier key so `ClaudeDriver` can resolve it again. The round trip is a subclass whose only job is undoing work
reason: The shim is a current protocol adaptation: supervisor LaunchRequest.model is the concrete resolved model, while the existing adapter accepts configured tier keys. Passing route.tier as suggested contradicts the supervised request contract. The provider-edge conversion has a present architectural purpose; no incorrect mapping or changed behavior was demonstrated.

issue: `DEFAULT_PHASE_TIERS = {"build": "sonnet", "review": "opus", ...}` lives in the provider-neutral `ovcaq.drivers` package init and feeds `config._supervisor_phases`. Neutral routing defaults are therefore Claude tier names: any agent without `sonnet`/`opus` tier keys fails with "Unknown agent tier" (AGENTS.md: model names live under their adapter)
reason: sonnet/opus here are configured logical tier keys, not provider model identifiers. The accepted design explicitly specifies these defaults, and custom agents can set phase tiers mapped to arbitrary provider model IDs. Unknown-tier rejection is required validation. Moving them into one provider would introduce coupling rather than fix a defect.

issue: Nothing in `src/` reads `SupervisorSettings.phases`. The supervisor routes through `resolve_phase_route(root, …)`, which rebuilds settings from disk (parsing both TOML files twice per call). So the validated `phases=` override and the `**explicit: object` runtime type checks in `supervisor_settings` only matter to tests
reason: Verified in current source and within PRD 00007; bounded regression task carries this finding verbatim.

issue: `_boundary` is a second, pre-launch decision table outside decision.py. It imports the private `_capability_decision` and ignores the `control.attention` that `decide` halts on, so a non-drained state with attention launches a session before halting (PRD: every halt is a pure, table-tested decision)
reason: Verified in current source and within PRD 00007; bounded regression task carries this finding verbatim.

issue: Every lifecycle failure (unknown agent, live capability owner, unavailable runner, unverifiable or failed stop) maps to `runtime_format`. Callers cannot tell "retry later" from a config error

issue: `ovcaq run` never calls `driver.probe()` (`build_driver` skips discovery and probe), so a missing agent binary shows up as a spawn exception after session evidence already exists
